name: FAIR Data
title: FAIR Data
answer: FAIR data is a set of principles for making research data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable by both people and machines. It applies to datasets, metadata, code, and other research outputs held in repositories and data archives. The principles do not require data to be open, only that conditions for access and reuse are clearly stated. In AI research, FAIR data supports reproducibility and the training or evaluation of models where data provenance matters.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: FAIR data is a set of principles for making research data findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable by both people and machines. It applies to datasets, metadata, code, and other research outputs held in repositories and data archives. The principles do not require data to be open, only that conditions for access and reuse are clearly stated. In AI research, FAIR data supports reproducibility and the training or evaluation of models where data provenance matters.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: FAIR data typically lives in institutional or disciplinary repositories, data catalogues, and persistent identifier systems such as DOIs and ORCID. Metadata is stored in structured schemas and exposed through standard protocols like OAI-PMH or REST APIs. Indexers and harvesters aggregate records across repositories, while controlled vocabularies and ontologies help machines resolve terms. Storage may be local, cloud-based, or federated, but the key infrastructure is the combination of persistent identifiers, rich metadata, and resolvable access paths.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Making data FAIR involves assigning persistent identifiers, describing datasets with community-standard metadata, and using machine-readable formats and vocabularies. Data stewards and researchers document provenance, licensing, and variable definitions at the point of deposit. Repositories validate metadata against schemas and expose it for indexing. The work is often done through data management plans, curation workflows, and automated checks that flag missing identifiers or non-standard fields.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: FAIR data carries rights and risks around ownership, consent, privacy, and reuse. Licences such as Creative Commons or bespoke data use agreements state what others may do, and provenance records track who created or modified the data. Sensitive data may be FAIR through mediated access, where metadata is public but the data itself requires approval. Risks include re-identification, misuse, and unclear attribution, so governance focuses on transparent conditions and audit trails rather than open access by default.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: FAIR data is moving toward machine-actionable metadata, where automated agents can discover, assess, and combine datasets with less human intervention. Repository networks are aligning on common schemas and APIs, and AI systems are beginning to use FAIR metadata for data selection and bias checks. The next stage is likely tighter links between data, code, models, and publications, with provenance captured at finer granularity. Progress depends on sustained curation effort and incentives for researchers to invest in reusable data.
